title: Lina and the Mixed-Up Flags
markdown:
It was a bright clear morning. Dew drops sparkled like tiny diamonds on every blade of grass. The air smelled sweet, like clover. Lina, who loved to build and fix, was taking a stroll with her friends, Sunny the squirrel and Dr Sol the wise tortoise.

Lina had clever hands and a curious mind. She could mend a robin’s nest or help a wobbly mushroom stand tall. Sunny, twitching whiskers and bushy tail, was full of buzzing energy. He spotted everything. Dr Sol, shell warm like a sun-baked pebble, moved slowly and thoughtfully. His eyes held the wisdom of many seasons. They were on their way to the Little Acorn Picnic spot, a favourite clearing for delicious fallen acorns.

When they reached the winding path, something puzzling had happened. The path was usually so clear, marked by cheerful garden flags that fluttered like little dancers. Today the flags were a jumble. Red flags tangled with blue, yellow with green, purple with orange. The colourful mess hid the path. Lina gently tried to pull a red flag, but it tugged back, stuck to a bright blue one. Her brow furrowed a tiny bit. Sunny scampered up a bush. “It’s all mixed up!” Dr Sol blinked slowly. “The way forward is hidden when it is so confused.”

Lina sat on a soft patch of moss. The forest hummed gently around her. A fern uncurled, unhurried. She looked at the tangled flags, then at Sunny’s eager face and Dr Sol’s calm gaze. She noticed how the red flags were all in one big clump, and the blue flags in another, though tangled within their own colours.

She sat very still for a moment, watching a ladybug slowly climb a blade of grass. The world around her was quiet, waiting. Clouds did nothing in particular, which was just right. Sunny almost spoke, then didn’t. That was a kindness too.

“Look,” she said softly, pointing a gentle finger. “The red flags are all together, and the blue flags are all together, even though they are tangled within their own colours. What if we helped them find their own colour families?”

Sunny’s tail gave a happy energetic flick. “Colours! We can put all the reds in one pile, and all the blues in another. That will make them less mixed.” Lina smiled, her worry fading like mist. She carefully picked up a bright red flag, then another, and another. She laid them down side by side on the soft grass. Soon a small neat pile of bright red flags grew. “See. Now we can see the path where they were.”

Sunny darted around, helping. He nudged a yellow flag towards Lina’s growing pile of yellows. Dr Sol steadied stray green flags with his nose, guiding them to Lina’s green pile. They worked with gentle hands. They sorted the yellow flags, then the green, then the purple, and then the little orange ones. Each colour had its own neat family.

As they finished the last of the purple flags, the path, which had been completely hidden, became clear and easy to follow. It stretched out, bright and inviting. Lina let out a quiet sigh of satisfaction. “By sorting the flags by their colour, we could see them, and it was much easier to untangle them all.”

Dr Sol nodded, wise old eyes twinkling. “When things are sorted, their purpose becomes clear. Colour helps us see the world. Think of the rainbow after a gentle rain, how each colour sits next to its neighbour.”

Sunny chirped. “I wonder what other patterns are hiding, just waiting for us to sort them out. Are there patterns in the clouds? Or in the seeds the birds eat?”

With the path clear and their hearts full of a gentle discovery, they stood a moment longer. The flags, in their colour families, looked like a quiet rainbow laid on the grass. Then Lina, Sunny, and Dr Sol continued on their way, ready for their picnic, wondering what new patterns the world might show them, waiting to be sorted.
characters: Lina (a gentle engineer), Sunny (a squirrel), Sol (a tortoise)
